gloss: mama bike; utility bicycle with a basket

definitions.gloss: mama bike; utility bicycle (with basket and child seat)
definitions.explanation: A practical city bicycle with a low frame, a front basket, and often one or two child seats. The default bike type for everyday shopping, school runs, and short errands in Japan.

examples.japanese: ママチャリで{買|か}い{物|もの}に{行|い}く。
examples.english: I'll go shopping on the mama-bike.

examples.japanese: {前|まえ}と{後|うし}ろにかごのついたママチャリを{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought a mama-bike with baskets in front and back.

examples.japanese: {保育園|ほいくえん}の{送|おく}り{迎|むか}えには{電動|でんどう}アシスト{付|つ}きのママチャリが{便利|べんり}だ。
examples.english: For dropping off and picking up at daycare, an electric-assist mama-bike is very convenient.

notes:
Casual compound of ママ (mom) + チャリ (bike, slang for {自転車|じてんしゃ}). Despite the name, used by anyone — students, men, grandparents — not only mothers.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {電動|でんどう}ママチャリ: electric-assist mama-bike
- ママチャリに{乗|の}る: to ride a mama-bike
- ママチャリで{送|おく}り{迎|むか}え: to do school / daycare runs by mama-bike
- ママチャリの{前|まえ}かご: the front basket of a mama-bike

CULTURAL NOTE:
The ママチャリ is a Japanese icon: cheap, sturdy, three-speed at most, and built for short flat-city trips. Common features include a frame low enough to step through in a skirt, a basket large enough for grocery bags, a wheel lock, and front/rear child seats. Distinguishes itself sharply from sports bikes (ロードバイク) and folding bikes ({折|お}り{畳|たた}み{自転車|じてんしゃ}).
